assertions.assert: Each element takes exactly its declared attributes, the required ones present, and no content, and the namespace has no other element: a malformed element raises error.execution and assigns nothing (its schema, package/decision.xsd, rejects it before any run under scx validate).

<decision:choice> writes one choice {event, schema, description?} per event named by an active transition that carries an event:schema, in document order, each offered once (an earlier transition of the same state takes it); * and schemaless transitions are not offered, the description is the schema's description, else its title, first line, and events keeps only the choices a descriptor matches.
A transition whose cond is exactly true is offered; one whose cond is false is not.

<decision:compact> drops $schema, title and examples at every schema level, keeping property names; over the bound it drops every description, and still over it writes [], with overlocation true exactly when it wrote [].

<decision:pin> sets the values as the enum of the named property of every entry for the event, removes those entries when the values are empty, and raises error.execution, assigning nothing, for an entry whose schema has no such property.

<decision:assemble> writes the document's own choices untagged, then each offer's choices in member-name order tagged with the member's name as target, compacted, with its size and whether it is over the bound.

<decision:route> places each selection on the target it names when that target offers the event, else on the event's only offerer (null for the document's own); a selection that cannot be placed fails all of them with the original's message and an empty placement.
<decision:names> writes the choices' events, event@target for a targeted one, space separated.

<decision:selection> writes the original's dispatch tool as one schema: its description as the root description and its parameters {events: [anyOf one branch per offered event]} with the original's descriptions and examples; each branch {event, data, reason?, target?} has event a one-value enum, data the choice's schema without $schema (an empty object for none, wrapped as value for a non-object), required only when the schema requires a field, the schema's description else the event name, and target, required, a sorted enum of the offering targets only when one has a target; nothing is normalized for strict decoding.

<decision:tuner> keeps the original's ConfidenceTuner state {mean, var, n}: anything else is replaced by the initial state, an observation moves it, and the threshold is the floor during the warmup, else max(floor/2, mean - k_sigma * deviation), as a probability; an observation that is not a number raises error.execution and assigns nothing.
A location that does not hold what the element reads raises error.execution and assigns nothing.
